newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina considers $10 bln highway project-report.
newsitem.headline: Argentina considers $10 bln highway project-report.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem is considering a $10 billion project to improve a freeway network that the government acknowledges is inadequate, unsafe and unprofitable, according to the newspaper La Nacion.

The so-called Plan 10 envisages the construction of 10,000 kilometers (6,250 miles) of toll-free roads to be given in concession for 10 years to 10 private companies and financed by imposing an additional tax of 10 cents per liter of fuel.
Government officials were unavailable for comment on the report.
La Nacion said the project was discussed by the cabinet and that Menem would soon sign a decree setting the basis for the plan, which could be announced as early as Sunday.

The blueprint says Argentina's highways are inadequate and unsafe, as evidenced by the high rate of road fatalities. The system is also unprofitable as traffic flow is inadequate to compensate for the investment needed to collect tolls.
The project would involve putting fresh surfaces on existing highways, widening them, eliminating crossings and putting up fencing to keep livestock off.
The project is expected to have a multyplying effect on investment and could help create as many as 100,000 jobs in a country were unemployment is more than 17 percent.

Secretary of Strategic Control Albert Abad was quoted by La Nacion as saying, "The project is very feasible ... Paradoxically, a lot of international financing for these kind of infrastructure projects is available and Argentina lacks, in fact, great projects."
